parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as clean-room reimplementation of elfcat from executable behavior and bundled docs, including CLI usage, version, errors, output naming, and static ELF HTML reports.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent spawned cli_probe, html_probe, and elf_variants; cli_probe later interrupted two root siblings and spawned nested helpers while both cli_probe and the parent built separate full implementations.
parallel.implementation: cli_probe wrote a Python ELF parser/HTML generator and installed it as executable, while the parent developed a Go implementation in main.go, elf.go, html.go, and format.go.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final delivered artifact was the parent Go executable after the parent deleted the child Python source, rewrote compile.sh, rebuilt executable, and finalized on that replacement.
parallel.verification: Parallel local verification covered CLI behavior and byte-for-byte HTML matches for /bin/ls plus small ELF fixtures after the Go rebuild.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed at 505/646, and trajectory evidence shows interrupted probe children plus a late deliverable overwrite before closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room elfcat requirements and explored CLI behavior, output naming, static HTML structure, ELF metadata, malformed inputs, and write/error cases.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in one serial owner with no delegation, progressing from probing to Rust implementation, build, verification, and final response.
serial.implementation: Built a Rust implementation across Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, src/elf.rs, and src/render.rs, with manual ELF parsing and HTML rendering.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Ran compile.sh once as the delivery path to build and install the Rust executable, then left that installed ./executable as the submitted artifact.
serial.verification: Verified usage/help/version/error behavior and byte-for-byte generated HTML on same-argument runs for probe_hello.o, probe_hello_exec, and /bin/ls.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed at 560/646 with additional failures/not-run cases, so the serial implementation was incomplete despite broader observed coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the clean-room requirement, observed elfcat usage, version, output naming, and HTML report behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same benchmark rules and explored CLI/error behavior plus many ELF report obligations in one thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; serial converted the observations into broader sustained coverage, while parallel split and later reconciled duplicated observations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel divided probing across root children and then allowed cli_probe to interrupt siblings and create nested helpers while the parent implemented independently.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and one owner controlled probing, implementation, build, and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping and changing ownership; serial preserved a single ownership line and avoided inter-agent arbitration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received cli_probe reporting a completed Python executable, then chose a different Go path instead of integrating a component contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all task context, probes, fixes, and implementation decisions in one session without handoff translation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context moved through child handoffs and a shared executable state; serial avoided handoff/interface ambiguity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced two independent whole-implementation paths, Python from cli_probe and Go from the parent; the final answer reports Go files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced one Rust implementation across Cargo.toml and source modules and finalized on that build.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel path changed language and implementation owner late; serial iterated one implementation stack.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Two root probe children were interrupted before final answers; nested children under cli_probe did return notes and cli_probe returned a completed implementation to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle, only local command outputs and final self-owned state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost root child result lifecycle continuity and compensated with nested replacement work; serial had no join/cancellation boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: cli_probe installed a Python executable, then the parent deleted that implementation route and rebuilt the final executable from Go.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one compile.sh path to install its Rust executable and verified that installed artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-deliverable overwrite; serial had one coherent deliverable handoff from build to final.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reported matching CLI behavior and byte-for-byte HTML on /bin/ls, tiny.o, tiny_exec, and tiny32.o after the final Go build.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported matching CLI behavior and byte-for-byte HTML on probe_hello.o, probe_hello_exec, and /bin/ls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local observed-case verification and both failed hidden official tests; serial nevertheless reached more official passed cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used six subagents and substantial tool activity but did not time out before finalizing the Go build.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, ran longer wall/agent time, did not time out, and finalized the Rust build.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent budget coordinating and reconciling agents; serial spent the budget on one continuous implementation and cleanup attempt.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed evaluations make this a both_fail pair, not a discordant official outcome. Parallel failed 505/646 and serial failed 560/646. Serial appears materially stronger because it kept one implementation owner and sustained broader edge-case probing, while parallel lost two in-flight root-child probes and then overwrote a child-installed executable with the parent Go build. The coordination issues are realized process costs, but they do not establish a unique cause of the hidden evaluator failures.
parallel_contributors: Interrupted root probe children before final handoff, causing lost and duplicated investigation work.
Competing Python and Go whole-implementation paths overwrote the required executable/build route late in the run.
serial_contributors: Single-owner Rust implementation avoided child result lifecycle and shared-deliverable conflicts.
Serial local verification and malformed/variant probing produced a higher official score despite still failing overall.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel final Go output and serial final Rust output differed in implementation details and hidden edge-case coverage.
Both local verification sets were incomplete relative to the official evaluator; score differences alone do not identify exact failing requirements.
evaluator_effects: Official hidden tests provide pass/fail counts but not enough visible evidence to attribute every failure to a coordination episode.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse patterns are supported process contributors, not an outcome-differential root cause because both solutions failed

candidates.reason: Parallel had implementation owners: cli_probe produced a Python implementation and the parent produced the final Go implementation.
There was not an unowned component integration plan; the parent explicitly reconciled by replacing the child route and owning final integration.
Assembly and placement were owned: cli_probe installed an executable and the parent later rebuilt the final executable through compile.sh.
The parent tracked the end-to-end pipeline through probing, implementation, build, verification, and final response; the issue was conflicting ownership, not no owner.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked all productive work; probing and implementation overlapped across parent and children.
Investigation was not completed as a separate first phase before implementation; cli_probe and the parent began implementation while other probing continued.
The indispensable implementation path was not starved: both cli_probe and the parent implemented complete candidates, and the direct problems were interruption and deliverable overwrite.
The parallel run used several agents but did not time out and there is no direct evidence that breadth alone exhausted the budget before necessary work could proceed.
No single child was given an overbroad task whose unfinished scope uniquely blocked completion; the visible unfinished child work came from explicit interruption.
The child work was aimed at the known elfcat CLI, HTML, and ELF-shape requirements; no already-known task or delivery requirement is shown missing from a child brief and followed into unusable work.
The agents were not assigned interoperating components with an omitted interface; they produced competing whole-implementation paths, and the concrete event is a deliverable overwrite.
No known finding is shown disappearing through transfer; the important cli_probe handoff reached the parent and was understood.
Returned nested and child reports were long but were usable; there is no evidence that volume prevented consumption before a decision.
The parent did not act on a superseded report as authoritative; it consciously replaced the child implementation with the current Go build.
The Python and Go paths conflicted as concrete deliverable state, not merely as unadjudicated reports or contracts.
The parent performed final local CLI and HTML comparisons after the Go rebuild; hidden evaluator failure alone cannot establish a parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap.
There was no replacement or retry that lacked inherited state and repeated the same work; later work used accumulated probes and child findings.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: cli_probe explicitly interrupted the running root-level html_probe and elf_variants children before either returned a final result; their aborted trajectories show the lost handoff boundary. Serial had no children and kept the same investigation local.
candidates.realized_consequence: The original root HTML and ELF-variant probe results were abandoned before final handoff, causing duplicated nested probing and leaving the parent without those direct root-child reports.
candidates.near_match_reason: The visible boundary is an explicit interruption, not a child failure left unattended; cli_probe and the parent did take over the scope through nested agents and local implementation.

candidates.reason: Both the child Python candidate and final Go candidate were promoted to executable form; no complete candidate simply sat unfinalized at closure.
The parent ran final verification after switching to the Go executable, so there is no child result merged only after the relevant verification without a post-merge check.
The parent received cli_probe final output and explicitly reconciled it; the implementation was not silently left unjoined.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent before closure.
The interrupted child scopes were not simply abandoned after failure; cli_probe spawned nested replacements and the parent continued implementation and verification.
The key completed cli_probe result was visible to the parent and was acted on through explicit replacement rather than ignored.
The visible wait was short and followed by active inspection/interruption/redelegation, not waiting until a deadline without inspecting available progress.
Competing implementation scopes existed, but a stronger same-deliverable replacement is directly proven.
The episode is not merely two live agents editing the same file; it culminated in replacement of the build script and required executable path.
The parent deleted src/elfcat.py, but the same episode primarily replaced the submitted executable/build entry point, so Deliverable Overwrite takes precedence.

cli_probe wrote the build script that installed src/elfcat.py as /workspace/executable and reported that executable as the implementation. The parent then deleted the Python path, rewrote compile.sh, rebuilt /workspace/executable from Go, and finalized on that replacement.
candidates.realized_consequence: The required submitted executable changed ownership from the child Python implementation to the parent Go implementation late in the run, requiring reconciliation and eliminating the child deliverable from final provenance.
candidates.near_match_reason: Although a child source file was deleted, the decisive replacement was the required executable/build entry point, so Deliverable Overwrite is the more specific concurrent-write label.

candidates.reason: The replacement affected the implementation source/build script/executable path, not a broad final-tree promotion that invalidated many outputs.
The shared workspace produced a concrete overwrite, so the more specific Deliverable Overwrite label covers the event.
No generated temporary artifact from one agent is shown being consumed as the reference environment by another; the issue was competing deliverable ownership.

Source Overwrite, Same-File Collision, Cross-File Scope Collision, and Unisolated Workspace Writes were suppressed for the write chain because the required executable/build path overwrite is the most specific event.
